about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Japanese Chawanmushi Savoury Egg Custard
recipes.summary: Silky steamed egg custard in dashi with prawn and shiitake, set gently so it wobbles like soft tofu.
steps: Whisk the eggs gently with the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and a pinch of salt, then strain through a sieve into a jug so the custard is smooth.
Divide the prawns and shiitake between four heatproof cups and pour the egg mixture over, skimming off any bubbles.
Cover each cup with foil and set in a steamer over barely simmering water.
Steam on low for 15 to 18 minutes, until the custard just sets with a gentle wobble and a skewer comes out clear.
Scatter with spring onion and serve hot with a spoon.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no liquid egg, and the prawns until pink and opaque. Keep the steamer at a gentle simmer so the custard stays smooth. Eat the same day and do not reheat.

recipes.title: Japanese Okayu Egg and Spring Onion Rice Porridge
recipes.summary: Soft, gentle rice porridge simmered in dashi with a softly set egg, a comforting Japanese morning bowl.
steps: Put the rice, water and dashi powder in a saucepan and bring to the boil until bubbling, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is very soft and creamy.
Season with a pinch of salt and the soy sauce.
Beat the eggs and swirl them in, then cook for 2 minutes, until the egg is fully set in soft ribbons.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion, sesame oil and pickled ginger.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set, with no runny egg left. Eat the same day.

recipes.title: Japanese Salmon Ochazuke Dashi Rice
recipes.summary: Hot dashi poured over rice and flaked grilled salmon, a light and soothing Japanese supper.

items: 2 salmon fillets, skin on, about 120g each
1 sheet nori, cut in thin strips

steps: Season the salmon with a pinch of salt and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the flesh flakes easily and is opaque all the way through.
Flake the salmon into large pieces and discard the skin.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, nori, sesame seeds and spring onion.
Stir the soy sauce into the hot dashi and pour it over the rice until it is just covered.
Serve straight away with a little wasabi on the side.
notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque all the way through, then eat it promptly. Cool any leftover rice and refrigerate it within 1 hour, then use within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Japanese Kenchinjiru Root Vegetable and Tofu Soup
recipes.summary: A temple-style vegan soup of daikon, carrot, sweet potato and crumbled tofu simmered in dashi and sesame oil.
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and fry the tofu for 3 minutes, until lightly golden.
Add the daikon, carrot, sweet potato and shiitake and stir for 2 minutes, until glossy.
Pour in the dashi and bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and mirin and taste for seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Japanese Goma-ae Sesame Spinach
recipes.summary: Blanched spinach in a sweet, nutty ground sesame dressing, a classic cold Japanese side.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and blanch the spinach for 40 seconds, until bright green and just wilted.
Drain and cool under cold water, then squeeze out the water firmly with your hands.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar until mostly crushed and oily.
Mix in the soy sauce, sugar, mirin and vinegar until the dressing is smooth.
Toss the spinach through the dressing and serve in small mounds.
notes: Best eaten the day it is made. Chill for 20 minutes for a cooler side.

recipes.title: Japanese Hiyayakko Chilled Tofu with Ginger and Bonito
recipes.summary: Cold silken tofu with grated ginger, spring onion, bonito flakes and soy, a no-cook summer starter.
steps: Drain the tofu gently on paper towel for 5 minutes, then cut it into two large blocks.
Place each block on a plate and top with the ginger, spring onion and bonito flakes.
Drizzle with the soy sauce and scatter with sesame seeds and herb.
Chill until very cold, then serve straight away.
notes: Keep the tofu in the fridge until the moment of serving.

recipes.title: Japanese Ohitashi Greens in Dashi
recipes.summary: Blanched greens soaked in cool soy dashi, a refreshing make-ahead side with bonito flakes.
steps: Blanch the bok choy in boiling water for 1 minute, until bright green and just tender at the stems.
Plunge into iced water, then drain well and squeeze lightly.
Mix the dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a shallow dish.
Add the greens and soak in the fridge for 30 minutes, turning once.
Lift out, cut into short lengths and serve topped with bonito flakes and sesame seeds.
notes: Keeps in its liquid in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.title: Chinese Cong You Bing Spring Onion Egg Pancake
recipes.summary: Flaky, crisp-edged spring onion pancakes folded around a soft fried egg, a Taiwanese street breakfast.
steps: Mix the flour, boiling water and a pinch of salt into a shaggy dough, then knead for 3 minutes, until smooth, and rest under a bowl for 20 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls and roll each very thin, brush with sesame oil and scatter with spring onion and salt.
Roll up like a cigar, coil into a snail and flatten with your palm, then roll out to about 3mm thick.
Fry each pancake in a little vegetable oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and blistered with crisp edges.
Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your liking.
Place an egg on each pancake, drizzle with soy, sugar and chilli sauce, fold and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are completely set. Pregnant, elderly and young people should have the yolk cooked firm.

recipes.title: Chinese Marbled Soy Eggs
recipes.summary: Hard-boiled eggs cracked and simmered in star anise, wine and soy until the shells show a marbled pattern.
steps: Boil the eggs in water for 9 minutes, until the yolks are fully set, then cool in cold water.
Tap the shells all over with a spoon so they crackle but stay on.
Simmer the wine, soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, sugar, orange peel and water for 10 minutes, until fragrant and dark.
Add the eggs and simmer on very low heat for 40 minutes, until the colour has soaked in.
Turn off the heat and steep for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge, then peel to reveal the marbling.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set. Keep refrigerated in the liquid and eat within 4 days.

recipes.title: Chinese Dry-Fried Green Beans with Pork
recipes.summary: Blistered green beans wok-tossed with pork mince, garlic and preserved vegetable, a Sichuan favourite.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the beans for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing, until blistered and wrinkled but still crisp.
Remove the beans and add the remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry the pork mince for 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the beans with the soy sauce, wine and sugar and toss for 1 minute, until glossy.
Finish with the sesame oil and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre and no pink remains. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use in 2 days.

recipes.title: Chinese Doufu Nao Savoury Silken Tofu Pudding
recipes.summary: Warm, spoonable silken tofu in a soy, chilli oil and pickle broth, a northern Chinese breakfast.

items: 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps: Heat the stock, soy sauce and vinegar in a small saucepan until simmering.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute, until the broth is lightly thickened.
Slide the tofu in large spoonfuls into the broth and warm gently for 3 minutes, until just steaming.
Ladle into two bowls and top with peanuts, spring onion, chilli oil and sesame oil.
notes: Serve at once; the tofu breaks up if boiled hard.

recipes.title: Korean Kongnamul Guk Bean Sprout Soup
recipes.summary: A clear, clean soup of soybean sprouts and garlic, the classic Korean morning-after bowl.
steps: Bring the water and kombu to the boil until bubbling in a lidded pot, then remove the kombu.
Add the sprouts and garlic, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the sprouts are tender and no longer raw-tasting.
Stir in the soy sauce and fish sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the spring onions and chilli flakes and drizzle with sesame oil before serving hot.
notes: Keep the lid on while cooking to avoid a grassy taste. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Miyeok Guk Seaweed and Beef Soup
recipes.summary: Birthday soup of silky wakame simmered with beef, sesame oil and garlic.
steps: Soak the wakame in cold water for 15 minutes, until soft, then drain and cut into short lengths.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the beef for 4 minutes, until browned all over.
Add the seaweed and garlic and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Pour in the water and soy sauce, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Stir in the fish sauce and serve with the spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C in the thickest piece and until tender, with no pink. Cool leftovers quickly and use within 3 days.

recipes.title: Korean Ssamjang Dipping Sauce
recipes.summary: Thick savoury dip of fermented soybean paste, gochujang, garlic and sesame for lettuce wraps.
steps: Mix the doenjang, gochujang, sesame oil and honey in a bowl until smooth.
Stir through the garlic, spring onion and sesame seeds.
Rest 10 minutes in the fridge so the flavours meld, then serve with lettuce leaves, rice and grilled meats.
notes: Keeps in a jar in the fridge for 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Korean Gamja Jorim Braised Soy Potatoes
recipes.summary: Baby potatoes simmered in a glossy sweet-salty soy glaze until sticky, a staple banchan.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the potatoes for 4 minutes, until lightly golden on the cut sides.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, water and garlic and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Simmer uncovered for 15 to 18 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced and the sauce is sticky.
Stir in the honey and sesame oil and cook 1 minute more until glossy.
Scatter with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Good in lunchboxes.

recipes.title: Korean Dubu Jorim Soy-Chilli Tofu Slabs
recipes.summary: Pan-fried tofu slabs simmered in a garlicky soy and chilli flake sauce, a savoury banchan.
steps: Pat the tofu dry and fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden.
Mix the soy sauce, chilli flakes, sesame oil, garlic, sugar and water.
Pour over the tofu and simmer gently for 6 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until it thickens and clings.
Scatter with spring onion and serve with rice.
notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Korean Oi Muchim Spicy Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: Crunchy salted cucumber tossed with chilli flakes, garlic, vinegar and sesame, a fast no-cook side.
steps: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, vinegar, sesame oil and sugar into a paste.
Toss the cucumber with the paste, spring onion and sesame seeds.
Toss and chill until cold, then serve within 30 minutes while the cucumber is still crisp.
notes: Best eaten the day it is made.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Xoi Lac Peanut Sticky Rice
recipes.summary: Steamed glutinous rice with roasted peanuts, coconut and fried shallots, a Hanoi street breakfast.
steps: Drain the soaked rice well and toss with a pinch of salt and the sugar.
Spread on a steamer lined with baking paper and steam for 25 to 30 minutes, until the grains are translucent and tender.
Warm the coconut milk gently and fold half through the hot rice.
Pile into bowls and top with peanuts, shallots, sesame and a drizzle of the remaining coconut milk.
notes: Soak the rice at least 6 hours or overnight; this soaking time is not included in prep. Contains peanuts.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Chao Ga Chicken Congee
recipes.summary: Silky rice porridge with poached chicken, ginger and spring onion, the Vietnamese cure-all.
steps: Bring the stock, rice and ginger to a gentle boil and simmer, stirring often, for 30 minutes, until the rice breaks down and thickens.
Add the chicken and cook for 12 minutes, until it reaches 75°C in the centre.
Lift the chicken out and shred, then return it to the pot with the fish sauce.
Simmer 3 minutes more and loosen with hot water if too thick.
Serve topped with spring onion, coriander, fried shallots and pepper.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink. Cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Canh Bi Do Pumpkin and Prawn Soup
recipes.summary: Sweet pumpkin and prawn soup scented with spring onion and a touch of fish sauce.
steps: Heat the oil and fry the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the pumpkin is soft.
Lightly mash a third of the pumpkin against the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Season with fish sauce and pepper and top with spring onion and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque. Eat the same day, or cool quickly and keep for 1 day.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Nuoc Mam Pha Sweet Fish Sauce Dressing
recipes.summary: The bright sweet, sour, salty and spicy table sauce for rice paper rolls, grilled meat and noodles.
steps: Stir the sugar into the warm water until fully dissolved.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and taste, adjusting for sweet and sour.
Stir in the garlic, chilli and carrot and rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. High in salt, so use sparingly.

recipes.title: Thai Nam Prik Num Roasted Green Chilli Dip
recipes.summary: Smoky roasted green chilli, shallot and garlic dip from northern Thailand, served with raw and steamed vegetables.
steps: Grill the chillies, shallots and garlic under a hot grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until blistered, blackened in spots and soft.
Peel everything, discarding the burnt skins from the chillies and the stems.
Crush the garlic and shallot in a mortar until smooth, then add the chillies and crush to a rough paste.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and oil until well mixed.
Serve with cucumber, cabbage wedges, green beans and sticky rice.
notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Chillies are hot, so wear gloves when peeling.

recipes.title: Thai Kai Jeow Fluffy Thai Omelette with Rice
recipes.summary: Deep-fried-style puffy omelette seasoned with fish sauce and lime, served over jasmine rice with chilli sauce.
steps: Beat the eggs with the fish sauce, lime juice and cornflour until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok until shimmering, then pour in the egg from a height.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until puffed and golden underneath, then fold in half and cook 30 seconds more until set through.
Drain on paper towel and serve over the warm rice.
Top with spring onion and chilli sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until fully set with no liquid egg. Eat the same day.

recipes.title: Indian Upma Semolina Vegetable Breakfast
recipes.summary: South Indian savoury semolina porridge with mustard seed, cashews and vegetables, ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Dry-roast the semolina in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until fragrant and lightly golden, then set aside.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and cashews and fry for 1 minute, until the seeds pop and the nuts turn golden.
Add the onion, chilli, ginger and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Pour in the hot water and salt and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Stir in the semolina gradually and cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until thick and fluffy.
Finish with peas, lemon juice and serve hot.
notes: Contains gluten and cashews.

recipes.title: Indian Mint and Coriander Chutney
recipes.summary: Fresh green chutney of mint, coriander, chilli and lime for samosas, kebabs and sandwiches.
steps: Roughly chop the coriander including the soft stems, and wash the mint.
Blend everything with the water until a smooth green sauce forms.
Taste and adjust the salt and lime juice until bright and sharp.
Spoon into a jar and chill; use within 4 days.
notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze in ice cube trays for up to 2 months.
